chunks: Sahl, from Ibn Fazal, from Ali ibn Uqba and Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Saeed ibn Yasar, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Praise is to Allah. There became a sect of the Murji'ah, and there became a sect of the Haruriyyah, and there became a sect of the Qadariyyah, and you were named the Tarabiyyah and the Shi'a of Ali. But, by Allah, what is it except that there is Allah alone, without a partner, and His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), and the Progeny of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon them), and the Shi'a of the Progeny of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). And the people are none but them. Ali (peace be upon him) was the most excellent of the people after the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and the most worthy of the people to the people.' He said it three times.

key_terms.آلُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: The Progeny of the Messenger of Allah
key_terms.أَفْضَلَ النَّاسِ: The most excellent of the people
key_terms.أَوْلَى النَّاسِ بِالنَّاسِ: The most worthy of the people to the people
key_terms.التُّرَابِيَّةَ: The Tarabiyyah (a specific sect named after their leader)
key_terms.فِرْقَةٌ قَدَرِيَّةٌ: Qadariyyah sect (those who emphasize divine decree/predestination)
key_terms.فِرْقَةٌ مُرْجِئَةٌ: Murji'ah sect (those who defer judgment on sinners)

ai.seo_question: Who are the true Shi'a according to Imam al-Sadiq in this hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) contrasts emerging theological sects like the Murji'ah and Qadariyyah with the true Shi'a, defining them as followers of Allah, His Messenger, and the Ahl al-Bayt. He explicitly affirms Ali ibn Abi Talib's (peace be upon him) status as the most excellent and most worthy leader (Awla) after the Prophet, a concept central to Shia political theology. This narration serves as a foundational text for the doctrine of Imamate, linking spiritual authority directly to the Prophet's Progeny.
